brief: The plaza's roundel and the quay are the only paving in the town with no memory of anything. Two gaps, one subject, both re-priced on HEAD this pass. (1) `paveWear[]` records where feet cross STONE and the only thing that reads it is `drawPuddles`, so on a DRY day the desire lines are invisible — even though `groundBase` already darkens worn GRASS through `wear[]` under `if (t === GRASS)`. (2) `buildPuddles()` walks `pavedAt(x,y)`, which returns true only inside the lane band or the cross street's columns, so the plaza and the quay never hold water at all. Do both, in that order: darken walked stone in the cached ground the way worn grass is already darkened, then extend the standing water to these two regions. They must agree with the moss that already lives there — `mossShelterAt` reads WATER neighbours through `MOSS_WET`, so the joints that hold water should be the joints that go green.
successLooksLike: On a dry day the roundel shows the line people actually walk between the fountain and the quay, present at every camera because it is in the cached ground. An hour after a shower the same low joints are still holding water while the open roundel has dried, and the moss reads greener along them than across the middle.
avoid: No new per-frame pass: the dry desire lines belong in the ground cache, and the new pools go into the existing PUDDLES array — c189 says drawPuddles is already 0.94 ms of a 2.0 ms frame at 560 pools and culls nothing for the camera, so adding pools without a cull is a cost you must at least measure. Extending the moss CA's agreement across regions is a second-region problem: mask the neighbour mean by region id or the plaza's growth feeds the quay's creep. Read `pavedAt`'s own comment before widening it — it is deliberately off the GRID, not off `pavingAt`, which is a fall-through.
